question: Hi everyone, I want to use LLM to evaluate the quality of my synthetically generated data using GPT-4. I was wondering if I should use GPT-4 as the evaluator LLM or should I use a different LLM so that it does not bias its own generation. Can someone kindly explain the best practice right now for this? thanks!

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer directly addresses the user's question: using GPT-4 (the generator) as the evaluator of its own synthetic data introduces self-evaluation bias, so best practice is to use a different or dedicated evaluator LLM, or apply safeguards.
examples: Since your data is generated by GPT-4, using GPT-4 as the evaluator could bias scores upward; a different evaluator LLM is safer
Best practice: use a different LLM or a dedicated evaluation model for your GPT-4 synthetic data
The same LLM acting as both evaluator and evaluatee systematically diverges from human judgments

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer defines self-preference: an LLM evaluator rates its own outputs higher than texts from other LLMs or humans even when human annotators judge them equal quality, as documented in GPT-4 dialogue benchmarks and summarization studies.
examples: GPT-4-based dialogue benchmarks and summarization studies show LLMs rating their own outputs above equal-quality alternatives
Self-preference means the evaluator inflates scores for its own generations relative to human judgments

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer cites the systematic study of generative evaluators (BART/BARTScore, T5/T5Score, GPT-2, GPT-3/GPTScore) on summarization showing evaluators assign higher scores to content from the same underlying model across model sizes and fine-tuning settings.
examples: 'Narcissistic evaluators': BARTScore favors BART-generated summaries, T5Score favors T5, and so on across four models
Numerous variations of BART, T5, GPT-2, and GPT-3 in both generator and evaluator roles showed same-model content scored higher

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer specifies that self-preference is stronger when generator and evaluator match in fine-tuning configuration and model size, and that inflated scores are particularly pronounced in reference-free settings—the typical scenario for synthetic data quality evaluation.
examples: Matching fine-tuning settings and model size between generator and evaluator amplifies self-preference
Because you're evaluating synthetic data without reference texts, expect inflated scores from a GPT-4 evaluator

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer situates self-preference among other known evaluator biases, including length bias (favoring longer outputs even when erroneous) and position bias (favoring responses based on list placement rather than merit).
examples: GPT-4 tends to prefer longer outputs even when they contain errors
Position bias: evaluation scores depend on where a candidate appears in the input rather than its quality

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes specialized evaluator language models trained for diverse, fine-grained evaluation, such as Prometheus, which achieves human correlation on par with GPT-4 (Pearson 0.897 vs 0.882) with reduced length bias.
examples: Prometheus, trained on 45 customized rubrics, matches GPT-4's human correlation while showing less length bias
Training dedicated evaluator LMs on high-quality rubric-based data mitigates evaluator biases

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer lists protocol-level mitigations: length-controlled adjustments (AlpacaEval), prompting guidelines (1-10 star scale, no chain-of-thought, temperature 0, one attribute per generation), and position-bias countermeasures (bootstrapping, split-and-merge, multi-agent discussion).
examples: AlpacaEval's length-controlled adjustments remove the significant positive length effect in automated evaluation scores
Use a 1-10 star scale, drop CoT, set temperature to 0, and score one attribute at a time for reliability
Multi-agent discussion or split-and-merge reduces position bias

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer (optionally) distinguishes self-recognition—an LLM's ability to identify its own outputs—from self-preference, noting the two are conceptually independent under a prosaic interpretation of 'self': a model can prefer its own text without recognizing it as its own.
examples: An LLM can favor its own text without knowing it generated it; self-recognition and self-preference can exist independently
The 'self' in self-preference is meant prosaically, not requiring the model to represent itself
